skill.name: ai-voice-cloning
skill.description: Guides AI voice generation, text-to-speech, and voiceover workflows with the inference.sh CLI. It covers model selection, voice styles, pacing, long-form narration, and media workflows.
skill.summary: Generate AI narration and voiceover workflows using inference.sh TTS models.
skill.author: inference-sh

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms the quick start recommends a remote installer piped directly to sh, which is a critical supply-chain risk. Most external command alerts are Markdown fences, inline model IDs, or documented infsh examples, not executable skill code. The skill also has dual-use risk because it documents synthetic voice and talking-head workflows without consent or disclosure guidance.

remediation.issue: Remote shell installer in quick start
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-sh installation with a checksum-verified package manager flow or a clearly separated manual install link.

remediation.issue: No consent guidance for voice and avatar workflows
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit requirements for permission, disclosure, and lawful use before generating voices or talking-head videos.

remediation.issue: Sensitive data may be sent to hosted models
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to submit confidential, regulated, or third-party media unless their organization approves the workflow.

remediation.issue: Related skill installation commands are shown as shell examples
remediation.suggestion: Move related skill installation commands to plain text guidance and require user confirmation before any install action.

content.value_statement: Teams need fast narration without building audio tooling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh TTS workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists supported inference.sh TTS models and common voice choices.
Provides infsh CLI examples for narration, dialogue, podcast, and video voiceover tasks.
Shows chunking and media-merger workflows for long-form audio.
Explains speed and punctuation controls for pacing.
Connects generated speech to avatar and video workflows.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, account login, and network access.
Provides documentation examples; it does not generate audio by itself.
Does not include consent checks for cloned voices or avatar likenesses.
Uses hosted models, so sensitive text and media need review before use.

use_cases.title: Create video narration
use_cases.description: Plan voiceover text, voice choice, pacing, and media merge steps for short videos.

use_cases.title: Produce learning audio
use_cases.description: Convert course scripts into clear narration settings for lessons and accessibility content.

use_cases.title: Prototype podcast segments
use_cases.description: Draft multi-voice dialogue workflows and merge steps for sample podcast episodes.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a short voiceover
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a concise inference.sh voiceover plan for this script: [script]. Recommend one voice and speed.

prompt_templates.title: Match a voice style
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare suitable voices for [audience] and [tone]. Explain the best choice and pacing settings for the script.

prompt_templates.title: Plan long-form narration
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this long script into narration chunks, keep the voice consistent, and outline merge steps for final audio.

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-speaker workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-speaker production plan for [project]. Include voice choices, chunking, merge order, and consent checks.

output_examples.input: Create a friendly product update voiceover for a thirty-second video.
output_examples.output: Recommended a warm female voice, normal speed, concise phrasing, and a media merge step for the video.

output_examples.input: Turn a long course lesson into narration-ready audio segments.
output: Split the lesson into short chunks by topic.
Use one consistent voice and slightly slower speed.
Merge the generated segments with short crossfades.

output_examples.input: Plan a two-host podcast sample with distinct voices.
output_examples.output: Suggested separate speaker generations, different voice IDs, consistent pacing, and a final audio merge pass.

best_practices: Confirm rights and consent before using any real voice, likeness, or portrait.
Test several voices and speeds before producing the final audio.
Review scripts for private, regulated, or third-party content before sending them to hosted models.
anti_patterns: Do not imitate a real person without permission and clear disclosure.
Do not send confidential scripts or private media to hosted models without approval.
Do not run remote installer commands without verifying the source and integrity.

faq.question: Does this skill clone a specific person's voice?
faq.answer: It mainly documents inference.sh TTS workflows and voice choices. Specific voice cloning needs consent and model support.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it create audio without extra services?
faq.answer: No. It depends on the inference.sh CLI and hosted models.

faq.question: Can it help with long scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows chunking and merge workflows for long-form narration.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive content?
faq.answer: Use caution. Hosted voice models may process text, audio, images, or video outside your local environment.

faq.question: What should I verify before publishing audio?
faq.answer: Verify script accuracy, consent, disclosure needs, licensing, and audio quality.
